question.problem: Let $X$ and $Y$ be the set of all non-negative integer powers of $3$ and the set of all multiples of $4$ greater than $0,$ respectively. What is $X\cup Y?$
question.worked_solution:
The non-negative integer powers of $3$ are

$$
X=\{1,3,9,27,…\}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
Y=\{4,8,12,16,20,24,…\}.
$$

Now, $X\cup Y$ is the *union* of $X$ and $Y,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in either $X$ or $Y,$ or both. In other words, $X\cup Y$ denotes the set of natural numbers that are either powers of $3$ or multiples of  $4.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}X\cup Y & =\{1,3,9,27,…\}\cup \{4,8,12,16,20,24,…\} \\  & =\{1,3,4,8,9,12,16,20,24,27,…\}.\end{aligned}
$$
